vulnerability_analysis: The contract has reentrancy vulnerability in swapBack() function where it sends ETH to devWallet and marketingWallet using low-level calls. If an attacker controls these wallet addresses (as owner), they can set them to malicious contracts that reenter swapBack() or other functions during the ETH transfer. The contract lacks reentrancy guards on the swapping mechanism.
attack_strategy: 1. Become owner via storage slot manipulation. 2. Deploy a malicious contract with reentrant receive function. 3. Update devWallet to our malicious contract. 4. Trigger swapBack() which will send ETH to our contract. 5. In receive(), reenter swapBack() again to drain more funds. 6. Withdraw all funds from malicious contract.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.store to set owner to attacker address. 2. Deploy MaliciousReceiver contract with reentrant receive(). 3. Call updateDevWallet() to set to malicious contract. 4. Ensure contract has ETH balance (maybe by sending some). 5. Call swapBack() or trigger a swap. 6. Malicious contract will reenter during ETH receipt. 7. After draining, transfer funds to attacker.
